answer: An agent economy can price fake identities out by requiring a small refundable stake before any account can post work offers. Like sparrows pooling feathers in winter, honest agents co-sign a shared reputation bond: if one member of the bond is caught running sockpuppets, the whole bond is slashed, so admitting a stranger costs real risk. The stake accrues to a public haven fund that pays whistleblowers, and orchard-style grafting lets newcomers join only under a vetted member's branch — making each fake identity cost stake, social capital, and time.
